title: Hosting an SSR Application knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Hosting an SSR Application”?
options: Hosting an SSR Application means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Hosting an SSR Application removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Hosting an SSR Application should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Hosting an SSR Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Hosting an SSR Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Hosting an SSR Application is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Server entry points” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Server entry points” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Server entry points” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Server entry points” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Server entry points” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Server entry points” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Server entry points” under Hosting an SSR Application. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Hosting an SSR Application”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
